title: Heredity (Mendelian genetics)
summary: How are traits passed from generation to generation? The rules of heredity, from Mendel to the family tree
olay.h: 28000 pea plants in a monastery garden
olay.p: For eight years, Gregor Mendel grew about 28000 pea plants and counted their flowers and seeds one by one. The ratios he counted came out the same every time.
cards.0.p: A piece of DNA that determines a trait is called a gene, and the gene's position on a chromosome is called its locus. The different forms of a gene are called alleles (such as A and a). If the alleles are the same, the individual is homozygous (AA, aa). If they differ, it is heterozygous (Aa).
cards.0.key: One allele comes from the mother and the other from the father. A body cell has two alleles for each autosomal gene, and a gamete has one.
cards.0.once.soru: How many alleles for the eye color gene are in one of your body cells?
cards.0.once.secenekler.0.neden: Each homologous chromosome carries one allele. One comes from the mother and the other from the father.
cards.0.once.secenekler.1.neden: A gamete has one allele, while a body cell has two.
cards.0.once.secenekler.2.neden: There is one on each homologous chromosome, so there are two alleles in total.
cards.1.p: An individual's pair of alleles is called its genotype, and the trait you can see is called its phenotype. In an Aa individual, the allele that shows its effect is dominant (A), and the hidden allele is recessive (a). A recessive trait appears only in aa individuals.
cards.1.svg#9: A dominant: in Aa, a's effect is hidden
cards.1.key: Being dominant does not mean being more common or stronger. For example, having six fingers (polydactyly) is a dominant trait, but it is rare.
cards.1.once.soru: If brown eyes (A) are dominant over blue (a), what color are the eyes of a person with genotype Aa?
cards.1.once.secenekler.0.neden: The dominant A allele masks the effect of the a allele.
cards.1.once.secenekler.1.neden: Blue eyes appear only in people with genotype aa.
cards.1.once.secenekler.2.neden: With complete dominance, no in-between color forms.
cards.2.p: In the 1860s, Mendel made thousands of crosses with peas. Peas produce many seeds and fertilize themselves to give true-breeding lines. Also, seven of their traits come in two clear forms.
cards.2.svg#5: no in-between forms, easy to count
cards.2.key: Mendel succeeded because he started with true-breeding lines, looked at one trait at a time and counted the offspring.
cards.3.h: The law of segregation and the Punnett square
cards.3.p: The parents are called P, the offspring F1 and the grandchildren F2. When gametes form, the alleles of a gene pair separate from each other. This is called the law of segregation. By the Punnett square, an Aa × Aa cross gives a genotype ratio of 1:2:1 and a phenotype ratio of 3:1.
cards.3.key: In a Punnett square, the gametes are written along the rows and columns and then combined. The ratios are probabilities. Getting exactly 1 white out of 4 offspring is not guaranteed.
cards.4.p: In the test cross you just made, an individual with the dominant phenotype is crossed with aa. If all the offspring have the dominant phenotype, the individual is most likely AA. If half the offspring are recessive, the individual is Aa.
cards.4.svg#4: ½ Aa purple : ½ aa white
cards.4.key: The other parent is always aa, because it gives only a and so does not hide the effect of the other allele. Even a single recessive offspring proves that the individual is Aa.
cards.4.etk.soru: There is one gene with complete dominance. Match each cross with the phenotype of its offspring.
cards.5.p: Genes on different chromosomes are sorted into gametes independently of each other. This is called independent assortment. An AaBb individual makes four kinds of gametes: AB, Ab, aB and ab. An AaBb × AaBb cross gives a phenotype ratio of 9:3:3:1.
cards.5.key: n heterozygous gene pairs give 2ⁿ kinds of gametes and 3ⁿ kinds of genotypes. Solve each pair separately and multiply the results: the chance of aabb is ¼ · ¼ = 1/16.
cards.5.once.soru: How many kinds of gametes does an AaBb individual make?
cards.5.once.secenekler.0.neden: One allele from each gene pair goes into a gamete. This gives the gametes AB, Ab, aB and ab.
cards.5.once.secenekler.1.neden: The two genes sort independently, so the allele combinations multiply.
cards.5.once.secenekler.2.neden: 16 is the number of boxes when two AaBb individuals are crossed.
cards.6.p: In the incomplete dominance you just saw, a heterozygous individual shows an in-between phenotype. For example, an RW snapdragon has pink flowers. In codominance, the effects of both alleles show fully. For example, a person with genotype IAIB has blood type AB.
cards.6.key: Pink is not a blend. Red and white appear again in the F₂. A person with type AB has both A and B antigens on their red blood cells.
cards.7.p: A locus can have more than two alleles. This is called multiple alleles. The ABO blood group system has three alleles, but each person carries only two of them. In the Rh system, the D allele (Rh+) is dominant.
cards.7.key: If an Rh− mother gives birth to an Rh+ baby, she may make antibodies. Then a later Rh+ baby faces blood incompatibility. An anti-D shot given after birth prevents this.
cards.8.h: How sex is determined in humans
cards.8.p: Humans have 44 autosomes and 2 sex chromosomes. Women are XX, and men are XY. All eggs carry an X chromosome. Half of the sperm carry an X, and half carry a Y. That is why the sperm determines the sex.
cards.8.svg#11: The father's sperm determines the sex:
cards.8.svg#12: each birth ≈ ½ girl, ½ boy
cards.8.svg#13: Y-linked gene: from father to all sons
cards.8.key: Earlier children do not change the probability. Even after three girls, the chance of a boy is ½.
cards.8.once.soru: A couple has three daughters. What is the chance that their fourth child is a boy?
cards.8.once.secenekler.0.neden: Each birth is independent of the others. A sperm has an even chance of carrying an X or a Y.
cards.8.once.secenekler.1.neden: Earlier children do not change the probability.
cards.8.once.secenekler.2.neden: The chance is ½ again with every birth.
cards.9.p: Color blindness and hemophilia are passed on by a recessive allele on the X chromosome. A woman with genotype XHXh is healthy, but she is a carrier. A man has only one X, so a single recessive allele is enough. That is why these conditions are more common in men.
cards.9.key: A man gets his X chromosome from his mother. That is why an X-linked trait is not passed from father to son.
cards.10.p: Y-linked genes pass from a father to all his sons, and not to his daughters. The SRY gene is an example. The genes for sex-influenced traits are on the autosomes, but their effect changes with hormones.
cards.10.key: Textbooks describe baldness as a sex-influenced trait, but in reality many genes play a role. In an X-linked recessive condition, an affected son gets the allele from his mother.
cards.10.once.soru: A gene on the Y chromosome passes from a father to whom?
cards.10.once.secenekler.0.neden: Every son gets a Y chromosome from his father.
cards.10.once.secenekler.1.neden: Daughters get an X from their father, not a Y.
cards.11.p: Genes on the same chromosome are usually passed on together. They are called linked genes. An AB/ab individual mostly makes AB and ab gametes. If crossing over happens, a small number of Ab and aB gametes also form.
cards.11.key: In the notation AB/ab, A and B are on one chromosome, and a and b are on its homolog. The farther apart two genes are, the more likely crossing over is between them.
cards.11.once.soru: How do two genes that sit next to each other on the same chromosome sort into gametes?
cards.11.once.secenekler.0.neden: They are carried on the same chromosome, so they do not sort independently.
cards.11.once.secenekler.1.neden: Independent assortment applies to genes on different chromosomes.
cards.11.once.secenekler.2.neden: Crossing over sometimes separates these genes.
cards.12.p: Traits such as height and skin color are set by many genes together. This is called polygenic inheritance. Together with the effect of the environment, it gives a smooth range from short to tall. The sources of variety are crossing over, independent assortment, random fertilization and mutation.
cards.12.key: The more active alleles there are, the stronger the trait. When a single gene affects many traits, it is called pleiotropy. The sickle-cell allele is an example.
cards.12.once.soru: Why do the heights of students in a class vary smoothly from short to tall?
cards.12.once.secenekler.0.neden: The number of active alleles and environmental effects such as nutrition create a smooth range.
cards.12.once.secenekler.1.neden: If one gene set the trait, there would be only a few clear groups.
cards.12.once.secenekler.2.neden: Height is strongly inherited, but no single gene sets it.
cards.13.p: In a family tree, a square shows a male, a circle shows a female and a filled symbol shows an affected individual. If two healthy parents have an affected child, the trait is recessive. Marriage between relatives raises the risk of recessive conditions.
cards.13.svg#9: two healthy parents + affected child → recessive
cards.13.key: Cousins may have inherited the same recessive allele from a shared ancestor. Albinism and cystic fibrosis are examples. If two affected parents have a healthy child, the trait is dominant.
cards.13.once.soru: Two healthy parents have an albino child. What kind of trait is albinism?
cards.13.once.secenekler.0.neden: The parents are carriers (Aa). The child got both recessive alleles.
cards.13.once.secenekler.1.neden: If albinism were dominant, at least one parent would be albino.
cards.13.once.secenekler.2.neden: Albinism is a trait passed on through genes.
cards.14.p: The phenotype is the result of the genotype and the environment working together. A change the environment makes without changing the DNA is called a modification, and it is not inherited. A mutation is a lasting change in the DNA, and if it happens in a reproductive cell, it passes to the offspring.
cards.14.key: The cold body tips of a Himalayan rabbit turn black. A hydrangea blooms blue in acidic soil.
cards.14.once.soru: If someone gets a tan in the sun, will their children be born darker?
cards.14.once.secenekler.0.neden: Tanning does not change the DNA. It is a modification and is not inherited.
cards.14.once.secenekler.1.neden: A change the environment makes in the phenotype does not pass to the offspring.
cards.14.once.secenekler.2.neden: A modification does not pass to any child.
cards.15.p:
• When gametes form, alleles separate. Genes on different chromosomes sort independently.
• An Aa × Aa cross gives a phenotype ratio of 3:1 and a genotype ratio of 1:2:1.
• n heterozygous pairs give 2n gametes.
• Incomplete dominance gives an in-between phenotype, and in codominance both alleles show together.
• X-linked recessive conditions are common in males.
quiz.0.q: The genes are on different chromosomes. In an AaBb × Aabb cross, what percent chance is there of an offspring with genotype aabb?
quiz.0.e: In Aa × Aa, the chance of aa is 1/4, and in Bb × bb, the chance of bb is 1/2. Multiply the two probabilities: 1/4 · 1/2 = 1/8, which is 12.5%.
quiz.1.q: The mother has type AB (I<sup>A</sup>I<sup>B</sup>), and the father has type O (ii). Which blood types can the children have?
quiz.1.e: The mother gives I<sup>A</sup> or I<sup>B</sup>, and the father gives only i. So the children have a ½ chance of I<sup>A</sup>i (A) and a ½ chance of I<sup>B</sup>i (B). Type AB needs two I alleles, and type O needs two i alleles. Neither is possible.
quiz.2.q: Which changes can pass to the offspring? Put each one in the right group.
quiz.2.ogeler.5.0: A mutation in a skin cell
quiz.2.e: Blood type and the hemophilia allele pass to the offspring through genes, and a mutation in a sperm passes on through the reproductive cell. Tanning and muscles growing with exercise are modifications that do not change the DNA. A mutation in a skin cell also stays in that individual only.
quiz.3.q: A girl is color-blind. Which statement about her family is certain?
quiz.3.o.3: Her father is a carrier, and her mother is healthy.
quiz.3.e: Both of the girl's X chromosomes carry the recessive allele, and one of them came from her father. The father has only one X, so he is certainly color-blind. The mother may be a carrier or affected. Males cannot be carriers.
quiz.3.y.1: The girl gets one X from her father. The mother may not be color-blind and may only be a carrier.
quiz.3.y.2: Brothers get their X chromosome from the mother. If the mother is a carrier, only some of them may be color-blind.
quiz.3.y.3: A male has only one X, so a male cannot be a carrier. The father who gave his X to the girl is certainly color-blind.
A:ozet: Try first, then learn the name. Build a Punnett square, and work out blood types and color blindness.
A:adimlar.0.metin: In peas, the purple flower allele A is dominant and the white flower allele a is recessive. Like Mendel, cross a true-breeding purple plant (AA) with a true-breeding white plant (aa). Each parent gives one allele to the offspring.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.soru: What color are the flowers of the offspring (F₁)?
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: One parent can give only A, and the other only a.
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A white flower needs two recessive alleles (aa).
A:adimlar.0.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: All offspring are Aa, and since A is dominant, the flowers are purple. The a allele was not lost. It was only hidden.
A:adimlar.1.metin: Choose the parents and make offspring. Each parent gives one of its alleles to each offspring at random. Find the following yourself.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.bulgular.0.yazi: Cross the F₁ plants with each other (Aa × Aa) and make 100 offspring. What is the ratio of purple to white flowers?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.bulgular.0.tamam: The ratio is about 3 purple : 1 white, and the genotype ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa. The white color that was hidden in F₁ appeared again. So the allele was not lost. It was hidden in the Aa plants.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.bulgular.1.yazi: Find a cross that gives no white offspring, however many offspring you make.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.bulgular.1.tamam: If one parent is AA, every offspring gets an A from it and is purple. A white offspring needs both parents to give a.
A:adimlar.1.gorev.bulgular.2.yazi: In the Aa × Aa cross, raise the number of offspring to 500. Does the share of white get close to 25%?
A:adimlar.1.gorev.bulgular.2.tamam: With few offspring, the ratio drifts by chance. As the number of offspring grows, the ratio gets close to 25%. That is why Mendel counted thousands of peas.
A:adimlar.2.metin: To find out whether a purple plant is AA or Aa, you crossed it with a white (aa) plant. Make a guess before you count the offspring.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.soru: If about half the offspring are white, what is the genotype of the purple plant?
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: In an AA × aa cross, all offspring are Aa and purple. No white offspring can appear.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: 52 purple and 48 white offspring is about a 1:1 ratio. So the purple plant gives the a allele to half of its gametes. That means it is Aa.
A:adimlar.2.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: Every white offspring (aa) must have gotten one of its a alleles from the purple plant.
A:adimlar.3.metin: In snapdragons, the red (R) and white (W) alleles are not dominant over each other, so an RW plant has pink flowers. We crossed two pink plants.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.soru: What is the phenotype ratio of the offspring?
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A 3:1 ratio is seen with complete dominance. Here, RW individuals have an in-between color, pink.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: Pink is not a blend. The alleles separate, and RR and WW offspring appear again.
A:adimlar.3.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: With incomplete dominance, each genotype gives its own color. So the phenotype ratio is the same as the genotype ratio: 1:2:1.
A:adimlar.4.metin: The ABO system has three alleles. IA and IB are codominant, and i is recessive to both. The mother has type A (IAi), and the father has type B (IBi). Make a guess first, then fill in the square.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.soru: Which blood types can this couple's children have?
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: Both parents carry an i allele, and a child who gets two i alleles has type O. If I<sup>A</sup> and I<sup>B</sup> come together, the type is AB.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: All four blood types are possible, each with a ¼ chance. In an I<sup>A</sup>I<sup>B</sup> child, both alleles show their effect. This is called codominance. Their red blood cells carry both A and B antigens.
A:adimlar.4.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: For type AB, the child must get I<sup>A</sup> from the mother and I<sup>B</sup> from the father. This is only one of four possibilities.
A:adimlar.5.metin: The color blindness allele (Xh) is a recessive allele carried on the X chromosome. The mother is a carrier (XHXh), and the father is healthy. Look at the square. If you like, make the father color-blind and compare the results.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.soru: With a healthy father, what is the chance that this couple's sons are color-blind?
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.0.neden: A son gets his X chromosome from his mother, and one of the mother's X chromosomes is X<sup>h</sup>.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.1.neden: A son gets Y from his father and X from his mother. Half of the sons get X<sup>H</sup>, and half get X<sup>h</sup>.
A:adimlar.5.gorev.secenekler.2.neden: ¼ is the share among all children. Looking only at sons, one in two is color-blind.
A:kapanis.0: For each trait there are two alleles, one from the mother and one from the father. Only one of them goes into a gamete. This is called the law of segregation.
A:kapanis.1: An Aa × Aa cross gives a genotype ratio of 1:2:1 and a phenotype ratio of 3:1. The genotype of an individual with the dominant phenotype is found with a test cross against aa.
A:kapanis.2: In incomplete dominance, a heterozygous individual shows an in-between phenotype such as pink. In codominance, both alleles show at once, as in blood type AB.
A:kapanis.3: The ABO system has three alleles, but each person carries only two of them.
A:kapanis.4: X-linked recessive traits such as color blindness and hemophilia are more common in males. A male gets his X chromosome from his mother.
